correctness.rationale: Primitive iid fair word has uniform least-rotation distribution on Lyndon representatives up to exponentially small periodic mass. With k≈(3/4)log2 n and ℓ≈5log2 n, pairwise ℓ-block collisions contribute O(n²2^(−ℓ)), absence of a length-k zero run is exponentially small in n^(1/4)/log n, and editing h−1 predecessors of the fixed 1 before the winning run can create a competitor only with probability O_h(n(log n)2^(−2k+h)), hence O_h(log n/√n). On the invariant good set the 2^(h−1) predecessor patterns are equiprobable; a fixed prefix is zeros. Independent disjoint trials and loss of only O(d) cyclic blocks at endpoints give interior saturation. Bounded-degree Hanf locality reduces every fixed FO sentence to finitely many boundary patterns, giving an effective dyadic limit and the convergence rate. FO disjunctions of terminal m-bit patterns realize every dyadic rational. Independent exact enumeration for lengths 2–16 verified Witt–Möbius Lyndon counts, boundary 0/1, and n=16 suffix profiles.
residual_risks: The finite enumeration illustrates only small lengths; unrestricted rate depends on the invariant local-switching bound and classical effective Hanf locality.
The n=16 suffix distribution is visibly not yet uniform, so it is not evidence for a sharp finite-n error constant.
